alerts.title: Possible EFV neuropsychiatric side effects
alerts.message: Sleep disturbance mentioned in notes for a patient on EFV. Reassure first. If the symptoms persist, consider substituting EFV with DTG (or LPV/r if a suitable DTG formulation is not available) (Uganda HIV Guidelines 2022, p. 269).

alerts.title: EFV CNS toxicity: insomnia and abnormal dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list persistent central nervous system toxicity (dizziness, insomnia, abnormal dreams) or mental symptoms as a major adverse event of EFV requiring management. Patient has been on EFV since February 2024 and now reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. These symptoms are classic EFV CNS side effects, and their persistence nearly two years after initiation supports drug attribution. No alternative cause is documented in the notes, though anxiety or depression should also be considered as guidelines note mental symptoms may overlap. The clinician's plan today does not address the likely drug cause or propose a substitution.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess symptom severity and consider substituting EFV per guideline toxicity management; evaluate for anxiety or depression before final decision.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend routine viral load monitoring at 6 and 12 months after ART initiation, then every 12 months for adults. The last recorded viral load was 60 copies/mL on 2025-08-10, 165 days before this visit, meaning the next annual viral load is approaching or due within months. No viral load order appears in today's plan. Continued routine virological monitoring is essential to detect treatment failure early and guide switching decisions.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule the next routine annual viral load test per the adult monitoring algorithm and document the result.

alerts.title: Plan lacks action for EFV side effects
alerts.message: The clinician documented insomnia and vivid dreams but ordered no medicines, lab tests, or regimen changes. Guidelines indicate EFV CNS toxicity warrants suggested management such as substitution, and EFV400 is associated with fewer adverse events than EFV600. The plan as written leaves a persistent, guideline-recognized toxicity unaddressed, risking treatment discontinuation.

evidence.recommended_action: Add explicit management of EFV CNS toxicity to the plan, including substitution or dose review per guidelines.
